top_categories.workout_context: Knysna Cycle Tour's rolling coastal road rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Knysna Cycle Tour's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before July.
At Knysna Cycle Tour, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Knysna Cycle Tour. Train it until it feels boring.
Knysna Cycle Tour's rolling coastal road forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 63 miles.
When someone attacks on rolling coastal road, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
63 miles on rolling coastal road burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Varied gradients on rolling coastal road demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
2-minute all-out efforts on rolling coastal road. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Knysna Cycle Tour, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Knysna Cycle Tour's rolling coastal road actually does to you.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Knysna Cycle Tour’s 63 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on TT Threshold, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 63 miles of rolling coastal road in Knysna Waterfront (Oyster Festival Grounds), Garden Route, Western Cape, South Africa.
